text: Commodore Vey, Tidewatch, Ironwatch station. State your business.
You again. I hope you've brought me something better than excuses.
Stand straight when you address an officer of the Tidewatch.
You've a price on your head and you walk into my fort. Either you've come to pay it, or you've come to hang.
Captain! Good to see you. The patrols speak well of you, and the patrols speak well of nobody.
I know your name, pirate. Speak quickly, and keep your hands where my marines can see them.
Listen to that thunder. Nobody sane is at sea tonight.
Storm's right on top of us. Stay in the dry a while.
Every timber in the harbour's groaning. Ugly night.
Wretched rain. Gets into everything.
Rain again. Good for the cisterns, bad for the soul.
You're dripping on my floor, by the way.
Late to be wandering about.
Night's when the cursed come walking. Keep a lantern lit.
Can't sleep either, eh?
Up with the gulls, I see.
Early start, {player}.
Mist'll burn off by mid-morning.

options.label: I'd like to settle my bounty.
What do you think of the Brethren?

text: Ironwatch Isle. Forty guns, two hundred marines, and the only dry powder magazine west of Kingsport.
From the north tower you can see three islands on a clear day. On a foggy one, you can see nothing, and that is when they come.
Ghost ships. Cursed crews. Pirates who think fog makes them clever. All three have learned the same lesson from my guns.
Order. Safe lanes for honest trade. Hangings for those who'd make the lanes unsafe.
And these days, mostly, putting the dead back in the sea where they belong.
Order. And for once, the dead are mostly staying down. I'm told I have you to thank. I don't enjoy thanking people.
Thieves with a constitution. Useful thieves, sometimes. When the cursed come ashore, the Brethren fight beside us. Then they rob us. It's almost a tradition.
You'd know them better than me, from what I hear. Choose your friends with care, captain.
